intro: How to open and close a message to a friend and an email to someone you do not know.
p.estimada.consejo: It is the formal greeting: «Estimada señora Ruiz:». For a man, «estimado». A colon follows.
p.querida.consejo: It is used with friends and family: «Querida Ana:». For a man, «querido».
p.le escribo para.consejo: It is the usted formula: «Le escribo para pedir información».
p.te escribo para.consejo: It is the tú formula, for friends: «Te escribo para darte las gracias».
p.adjunto.consejo: It is «adjuntar» in yo: «adjunto mis datos». The j sounds h: ad-HUN-to.
p.datos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «mis datos de contacto» are your phone and email.
p.un saludo.consejo: It is a correct closing for almost everything: neither too cold nor too warm.
p.un abrazo.consejo: It is used with friends and family. In Spain the z sounds «th»: un a-BRA-tho.
p.atentamente.consejo: It is the classic formal closing for letters and official emails.
p.gracias de antemano.consejo: «Antemano» means «ahead of time»: you thank before the answer arrives.
p.asunto.consejo: It is the line that sums up the email. It is written «Asunto: Información sobre el curso».
p.respuesta.consejo: It comes from «responder». You say «esperar una respuesta» and «dar una respuesta».
p.enviar.consejo: It is written with v, but sounds b. It is the same as «mandar»: «enviar un correo».
p.quedo a la espera de.consejo: It is a formal formula. A noun follows: «quedo a la espera de su respuesta».
b1.texto:
To a friend you write with **tú**: **Hola, Ana:** or **Querida Ana:** Then **Te escribo para…** and close with **Un abrazo** or **Un beso**.

To a company or someone you do not know you write with **usted**: **Estimado señor García:** or **Estimada señora Ruiz:** Then **Le escribo para…** and close with **Atentamente** or **Un saludo**.

Useful formal phrases: **¿Podría enviarme…?** **Adjunto** mis datos de contacto. **Gracias de antemano.** **Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.**

After the greeting, Spanish uses a **colon**, not a comma. Months are lowercase: mayo. And do not mix up **por qué** (question) with **porque** (reason).
b2.f0.texto: I want to write an email to a language school.
b2.f4.texto: I am writing to ask for information.
b2.f5.texto: Are you going to attach your details?
b4.texto:
The same message changes depending on who you write to:

- Friend: **Querida Ana:** · **Te escribo para** invitarte. · **Un abrazo.**
- Company: **Estimada señora Ruiz:** · **Le escribo para** pedir información. · **Atentamente.**

Other formal email formulas:

- **Adjunto** + noun: Adjunto mi currículum.
- **¿Podría enviarme…?**: asks politely for something.
- **Quedo a la espera de** su respuesta.
- **Gracias de antemano.**

After the greeting come a **colon**, and the text starts on a new line, with a capital letter.
b4.e0.texto: I am writing to thank you.
b4.e2.texto: I look forward to your reply.
b5.f0.texto: The desk lamp draws a yellow circle on the table.
b5.f1.texto: Pablo looks at the white screen with still fingers.
b5.f2.texto: A motorbike crosses the street and vanishes into the night.
b5.f3.texto: The cursor blinks slowly like a little heart.
b5.f4.texto: The first words finally appear on the screen.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo carefully writes each sentence of his message.
b5.f6.texto: His heart beats fast before pressing the button.
b5.f7.texto: The message flies along the invisible cable towards the school.
b5.f8.texto: A cool breeze comes in through the window and moves the curtains.
b5.f9.texto: Pablo leans back in the chair and breathes calmly.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! It is the formal greeting for strangers.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is too informal for a company.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is for someone close, not for a company.
b6.pregunta: You write to a company you do not know. Which greeting?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Le» goes with usted, the formal form.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Te» is for a friend, with tú.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Se escribo» is not said: the pronoun is «le».
b8.traduccion: I am writing to ask for information
b9.o0.refuerzo: Exactly: «un beso» is for family and friends.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is very formal; it fits an official email well.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is kind and neutral; it works for a formal email.
b9.pregunta: Which closing is too warm for a formal email?
b11.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Name, phone and email are your details.
b11.o1.refuerzo: The asunto is the email title; it is not attached.
b11.o2.refuerzo: The reply is sent by the other person later.
b11.pregunta: What do you attach to the email?
b12.o0.refuerzo: The closing goes at the end, not in the asunto.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Exactly! It sums up what the email is about.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That goes in the text, not in the asunto.
b12.pregunta: What is the asunto of an email?
p.formal.consejo: The stress falls on MAL, the last syllable.
p.contacto.consejo: The c before t sounds like «k». The stress is on TAK.
p.darte.consejo: From «dar». The «te» is stuck to the end.
p.escritorio.consejo: The stress is on TO. The io at the end is one syllable.
p.moto.consejo: Short for «motocicleta». The stress is on MO.
p.cursor.consejo: The stress falls on the last syllable, SOR.
p.parpadea.consejo: From «parpadear», to blink or flicker. The stress is on DE.
p.primeras.consejo: Plural feminine of «primero». The stress is on ME.
p.aparecen.consejo: From «aparecer». The c before e sounds like «th».
p.vuela.consejo: From «volar». The v sounds like b.
p.invisible.consejo: The stress is on SI. The v sounds like b.
p.cortinas.consejo: Plural of «cortina». The stress is on TI.
p.recuesta.consejo: From «recostarse», to lie back. The stress is on KWES.
p.estimados.consejo: From «estimar». Used in formal letters: «Estimados señores».
p.señores.consejo: Plural of «señor». The ñ sounds like «ny».
p.beso.consejo: The b and v sound the same in Spanish.
p.título.consejo: The stress is on TI, and the tilde marks it.
